purpose: Convert admitted literary/editing/research sources into transferable, conditioned craft intelligence without reproducing source prose or creating named-author imitation objectives.
distillation_rules: Distill mechanisms and decision rules, not stylistic surfaces or memorable phrasings.
A principle must state when it applies and when it does not.
Separate descriptive evidence from normative editorial preference.
Empirical results retain task/population/method scope; no universalization from one study.
Pedagogical or professional standards may define practice constraints but do not prove a literary effect in every genre.
A source can support measurement or evaluation without becoming training prose.
No external principle outranks protected canon, authorial intent, project voice, scene function, or protected language.
No principle may use named-author similarity as a target or success metric.
When evidence conflicts, preserve competing hypotheses and route to qualification rather than collapse to one rule.

confidence_model.HIGH: multiple high-fit authorities and/or strong empirical support with matching scope
confidence_model.MEDIUM: credible single authority or partially matching evidence
